en: I am surprised to learn that you are a mother, Moria. You must have been a very strict parent.
I can barely keep myself alive. What the hell would I do with kids?
I couldn't say. I hadn't seen them for years prior.
I do imagine that, yes.
I find that hard to believe. I can't imagine a warrior like you laying down with babes!
I had an orc uncle. One of my father's friends. They used to go fishing together, and then come home and tell me absurd stories of the gigantic fish they'd seen.
I imagine your children run barefoot and hunt beasts twice their size.
I see. You know, I've never really heard you talk about yourself.
I take it this doesn't bother you, then?
I understand it is rare for orc boys to know their fathers.
I wonder how long ago this was. I don't smell any traces of anybody but us, so it must've been a very long time ago.
I wonder what my dad was like.
I would have, yes, but that was a long time ago. You might imagine that I have a somewhat different view of the law now.
I'm pretty sure I can't have kids. Either that, or I'm lucky, and I know damn well that I'm not lucky.
I.. um... I suppose that's true.
I... see. Thank you.
In any case, being reminded of my sons does not require your belief.
Is it? You don't really know me at all.
It's good that you remember him. It's part of what keeps you human.
It's just about unheard of, actually. No sense worrying about it, I guess.
It's unbecoming of warriors to stand around and wax nostalgic over children, isn't it?
May I speak, Moria?
Mom must've been a talented woman if Dad's face really looked like that! Look at the size of that grin!
Most of the time orc men don't get to be dads. Those were some lucky kids. Look how happy they are.
Must everything always be about sex for you?
My papa was like that too. Big nasty swamp hog with a broken smile and mead in his veins.
My sons left my care when my eldest was twelve. His brother was ten.
Nah. Kids are great. Doesn't hurt to remember that.
No, though I did entertain the thought. I would have been pleased to raise such a strong-blooded child.
No. I raised them to be strong and to survive. My part is done.
Oh wow, you had kids? That's nuts!
Perhaps they do.
That must be hard being away from your family.
That's a... well I suppose it's a very practical perspective.
That's so cute! You can tell by the way this was drawn that this kid thought his dad was a hero.
The world is cruel, and will punish those who fail with starvation and death. I was considerably less strict than that.
Then you haven't a very good imagination. Who do you think raises those babes to be warriors?
They look happy, don't they? My children never did such things.
Twelve years?! Crap, is that how long it takes you guys to get that tall? I don't know how old I am exactly but I can't be more than... maybe eight? And I'm old for a goblin.
Two sons, yes. They would be nearly grown by now.
Useless rules writ by useless fools. 'Tis no country of mine.
Well, you're very mature for an eight year old, Borfalgor.
What was that, Moria? I couldn't hear you over the sound of thinking about sex.
Why wouldn't all human women choose orc husbands? They are undeniably superior mates.
Yeah.
You are too easily impressed, Rosaline. Even animals can raise children.
You don't need my permission to speak, Vankan. Do whatever you wish.
You have children? Goodness, that's a surprise.
You've got children?
Your countries have punishments for bearing half-orc children, don't they? I remember it happening a lot in my time.
Anybody else smell that? It reminds me of an old lady trying to cover an infection with perfume. Keep an eye out.
Byrne, are you alright? You seem bothered.
Guess there's not a lot to do when you're surrounded with nothing but workmen and trees, huh?
He took us all by surprise, Byrne. Don't beat yourself up over it.
Just a heads up, I smell flowers, and I smell it way too strong for it to just be regular flowers. Keep your eyes peeled.
Looks like a woodcutter's competition. Used to see a lot of these back in the days when the forest was more widely worked, or so I'm told.
Oh, I'm thinking of beating up a very specific someone over it, and it ain't me.
Someone really jammed that in there. I wonder if it's still any good?
Sorry. I'm still thinking about Vankan. I can't believe that bastard would betray us.
Figured this place would be my grave. I guess I'm lucky you found me before some hungry animal did.

I came looking for something... I don't remember. Just being too curious for my own good, maybe. Big guy grabs me from the darkness. I manage to get out of his grip and run back out, but I'm all the way outside before I realize he snatched the amulet.
I have nothing to offer you except for my thanks. I hope that you found something valuable inside, at least.

My name is Borfalgor. Surprised to see a goblin using proper speech? Can't say I blame you. That's part of what the amulet is for, I think. I don't really understand it, but without the amulet, I get stupid, and I get weak, and I probably die.
You're very kind. Thank you. I'll be fine in a moment.

Gloried one in sunken sea,
Lord Leviathan is he.
Hear our voices, dry above,
echo through the brine our love.
I will watch as you suffer and die.
The color of blood is pleasing to my eyes.

);

message(|
Come, then.
I have slumbered here in peace for decades undisturbed by man or beast, the darkness holding back any who might dare enter.
Now you presume your own invitation, intruding thus upon my home. I am awakened early, and my wrath stirs!
Still, my heart desires a brief distraction, and perhaps more sleep thereafter.
Then I shall sate my hunger with blood!
You, who leads the others! Offer yourself upon the bed. The others will wait outside. Ply my mood with thy flesh, and I shall let you leave in peace.
Build the kingdom for me and bask in its infant glory. Surely this is acceptable.
Go, meet with The Sunken One, and when he tries to destroy you, destroy instead the chains that bind him. Release his anchors, and I will treat with him myself.
He will not let you leave. He will never let you leave, and you will never be able to make him understand.
I am not interested in talking, Mortal. If you're here for the party, then enter the palace and present yourself to Lord Barrod.
I shall watch your battles from afar. If you decide to accept my offer, simply strike the chains. When they shatter, that will mark the signing of our contract. Simple, no?
I, however, can. My bargain for you is this.
Keep your distance, Mortal. I have no interest in harming you.
Now leave.
Soon, you will come up against something tremendous. Perhaps you know this already.
The Commanding Oak

The Sunken One will protect this island in your name for five-hundred years, and you will owe him nothing. No sacrifices, and no rituals. In return, I shall appear at the end of those five-hundred years to claim the island's crown for myself.

The Sunken One, he is like I am, a being that exists outside of the mortal space, but he is bound to it by great divine chains. These chains are his anchor, and his torment, and it is this torment that spurs his rage, causing him to lash out at you.
There are some others up on the eyrie, but I'll brook no nonsense in the archive. Through one door or another, leave.
Time to discuss your business, yes? Very well.

Welcome, Mortal, to my domain. I am Lord Barrod. Time is irrelevant here, so please make yourself at home and enjoy the party. Come and find me when you have had your fill of pleasure, and we shall discuss business.
You don't want to be here, Love. This party ain't even been started yet, haw.
You need not decide now. You cannot, after all, break the divine chains without my blessing.
You will gain absolute control over the island, and you shall become its ruler. This I promise.
Filthy swine!! What do you think you're doing here!?
A dirty story, hmm?
All that work, and then all the pressure to plant a girl in her, I don't need it! Why anyone would long for port when his sailors are beside him at sea is beyond me.
Alright, I'm in. What do I have to do?
Alright, Peregrine, that was my drink. My last drink. How many do you've left?
And what happens if I run out of whiskey?
And when I have the coin, I flip it, and you do the same?
Aye, one moment.
Before we came into port, we cracked open that barrel and we all took turns pumping our sweet nectar into it before sealing it back up, pretty as you please.
Captain! The game isn't - wow, Logus, your body is really - looking like a good body right now.
Captain, I could kiss you. Malkie is the one who got me shipped out here. Now, thinking about him with a belly full of sour sailors' pickles makes it all worth it.
Dammit! After a story like that, I'm gonna have to really step it up.
Did you hear something?
Didn't you wonder why none of my stories had comely maidens or busty wenches? Logus has never been pretty enough to even think about earning a wife, an' honestly, I couldn't be bothered.
Don't worry about it. We all act like cunts from time to time. Isn't that right, Logus?
Fine, I'll trust you.
Forget the coin. Finish your drink and drive me aground.
Glad to hear it. And by the way, I'm sorry I was such an asshole yesterday. I shouldn't offload my foul mood onto my friends. Forgive me.
Great. Time to bar the doors and hit the sack. I can't stay awake another minute.
Hah! Wrong!
Hah, Logus, you old ass. I'll get it.
Haw! It'll be you complaining when I'm the one putting you through the floorboards!
He really doesn't need to know. It'll serve him right for being a cunt today. It can be our little secret.
Heads!
Hold on a second, what's this?
I am not in the mood for another fight today. This place had better be clear.
I filled these glasses with the whiskey I found earlier. You've got six glasses, right?
I think that was his name! He was a pretty popular man to hate.
I'm listening.
If you guess right, then you get the coin. If you guess wrong, you take a drink, tell me something really dirty you've done, then you get the coin.
If you have no more whiskey left and you lose the coin toss, then I get your culottes. And if you got no culottes, I get you. On the floor. And no complaining.
Is that what you call sweet talk? And after you promised you'd play by the rules, too.
Just the old building creaking. Anyway -
Let's hope he doesn't find anything.
Logus, take a quick look down that hallway, and holler if you see anything.
Looks like we're clear, but there's a locked room at the end of the hall.
Oh yeah, just great!
Oh, Peregrine, luck of the devil, you have. We'll just be taking that.
Okay, so here's what we're going to do.
Okay, so there was this one time-
Patience, good Captain! I'm going to flip a coin, and you're going to guess what it lands on.
Please.
Right, on my way.
Right, six, and damn you for not just letting me drink it.
Right. Here goes!
Right. Lock taken care of. Coast is clear.
Shall we find out? Here's your first toss.
She really doesn't need to know. It'll serve her right for being a cunt today. It'll be our little secret.
That's amazing! Oh, please tell me it was Senator Malcolm!
That's so kind of you to say so! I'm so glad to be helpful!
There was one time that my crew and I hated this senator we were working for. I mean we really hated this guy. He was the highest, frilliest twat you ever saw.
This seems okay though. We can make this work until we get back to the stronghold.
Two? No, just one. One drink. It's my toss, right?
We appreciate your contribution, Peregrine. Just wanted you to know that.
We should know what's in there before we start taking our boots off. Peregrine, go check it out.
Well I thought I'd give my men a chance to skim the shipment too.
Well don't go thanking me yet! My toss now, remember?
Well for starters, you have to swear you're not gonna back down. I'm in this for keeps, and don't want to be disappointed if you turn out to be a quitter.
Well this damn island is my ship now, and this Captain's been lonely a wretched long time. Sailor, I need you!
Well, consider me sweet-talked. Who need rules anyway?
Well, while going over the shipping manifest for a job we were on, I notice there are a few barrels of expensive pickles bound for his estate. The good stuff with spices from south, you know?
What, you want me to swear on my heart or something? I am with you, and the boss will never need to know about it. Satisfied?
Wow, Peregrine, that was amazing! We'd never be able to make it through all this without you!
Wrong! Sud'o, Captain!
Yeah, I love those ones. It's no surprise he wanted to skim the shipment.
Yeah, that last one was a bit much.
Yes it is, so get over here and crash into it. I'm tired of waiting!
You got it!
You're so forward all of a sudden!
Adversity
Comraderie
A bed? Lad, you're the size of an ox. Just have her sleep on top of you!
A bed? Lad, you're the size of an ox. Just have him sleep on top of you!
Am I?
An old inn! Could be a decent place to camp.
An unlikely love blooming in the shadow of your criminal past. Honestly, I couldn't write a better tale if I tried.
Apologies, ma'am. Don't mean to upset you, of course.
Are you making fun of us?
Barbarian adonis? Damn.
Boss, I am so hungry right now and it is your barbarian adonis' fault.
But hey, if there's one here big enough, it's all yours!
Comfort here is fleeting. Let us finish our inspection so we may rest.
Damn. Now I'm putting some thought into it.
Do I ever! I know a guy. I'll introduce you later.
Do you have any idea how distracting it is when you start thinking about sex, Nazar? I can barely smell anything else.
Everything alright, Greave?
For later.
For me.

Grappling. No weapons. 
Or clothes. 
Best of three.
Hah! You've put some thought into this, I see.
Happy to help!
Have we got any oil?
Have you ever been out on a voyage at sea, Nazar?
I haven't ever even found a bed big enough to sleep in, let alone rut in.
I like my sandwiches with tons of pickles in them. Crammed in from every angle. More pickles than is reasonable, honestly.
I want so many pickles in my sandwich, Peregrine. Do you know where I can find some?
I was hoping to have room to curl my toes instead.
I was talking about sandwiches, thank you very much.
I'll do no such thing.
I'm glad you approve, Byrne.
I've known about you for a long time, but it just now occurred to me that you're both guilty of buggery.
I've known about you for a long time, but it just now occurred to me that you're both miscegenators.
If it's that hard to focus just do it over there. On the bench. We'll wait.
If there is, I'll fight you for it.
It's adorable how you sneak around and flirt in code like you think we don't know!
It's kind of hilariously stupid when you consider the things we lock people up for.
It's sweet that the two of you are finding some joy in all this mess, but really, now is not the time.
It... seems that's exactly what it is. Sorry for the confusion!
Know any orcish love songs?
Let her decide.
Let him decide.
Let's find some oil.
Making fun? Heavens, no, boy! Call me old-fashioned, but nothing stirs up the dust like a whirlwind romance! It's quite refreshing to watch it play out!
Nazar, you're joking.
No, Captain. Why?
No, Wisaka. He's joking.
No, dumbass, you smell amazing. It makes it hard to focus.
No, it's fine. I'm being a prude. Old habits die hard, it seems. Take such joy as you can find.
Now there's an idea!
Oh my God, you two are so cute I can hardly even stand it!
Oh, I wasn't planning to let it stop me.
Oh, double beds would be merrily welcome! I love having room to stretch your toes out!
Oh, no I don't think I know any orcish songs.
Oh, no reason. Just a thought.
Oh, this is good. This is important. There won't be a bed here. Not a double one, anyway, but don't let that stop you!
Oh. Well, thanks then.
Only for the sleepless soul in the tent next to yours.
Peregrine, you're not coming to bed with us.
Please bring empty bottles and steins indoors.
Please respect your fellow guests. No sex in the common room.
Rules?
Seein' your blood flow from one part of your body to another, there's a sorta poetry to it. It's kinda pretty.
Should I build one for you? Not here, I mean, but back at the stronghold? I can probably make something that would hold up to Nazar's... um... jumping... habits.
Sounds like you're the one who needs to get laid, Zan. Lighten up.
Surely you can carouse in private after our work here is done.
Thanks? I think?
That'd be swell, Bato! Maybe if we pick a permanent stronghold?
The bottom bun makes sure that none of the sandwich goes to waste. Sure, it gets flattened and abused, but the bottom of the sandwich is most certainly the happiest part.
Think they've got any double beds here?
Tonight's special - braised lamb!
Want me to sing a romantic song while you make passionate love? It'll be great!
We are still a thing, thank you kindly. I trust that's not a problem?
Well, learn a few, and maybe we'll take you up on it.
What use are curly toes? Is this an orc thing I don't know about?
What, are you saying I stink?
You go back to your room with a smile on your face, and the night feels a good deal more peaceful. You drift off to sleep quickly, and do not wake until morning.
You assemble outside the old tavern, and the morning is bright and dewey.
Peregrine and Logus are avoiding eye contact with one another, and they both stink of liquor.
The two of them look at each other for the first time this morning, and Logus clasps you on the shoulder.
If you've ever seen an orc blush as hard as Logus is blushing, you can't recall. Knowing what you know about how their night played out, you just grin and don't ask questions.
Logus clears his throat and averts his eyes for a moment, as he attempts to regain his composure.
You wonder if the two of them will be closer now, or if this was just a one-time thing.
He grins and waves you off.
He seems shocked to hear you say it, and just blinks, dumbfounded.
